episodes.163433: An area of low pressure developed across the southern Gulf of Mexico on Friday Nov. 5th and tracked eastward across north-central Florida Friday night, deepening offshore of the local NE FL Atlantic coast on Saturday Nov. 6th as strong surface high pressure wedged southward north of the region. This created a rare, true Nor'Easter event for the local area which including coastal and tidal flooding with inundation of 2-3 ft at high tides and damaging wind gusts, A High Wind Warning and Storm Warning for coastal and marine areas was issued. Localized heavy rainfall occurred for portions of coastal NE Florida. Moderate to major coastal erosion occurred. Coastal wind gusts of 40-50 mph started Friday morning then increased to 45-55 mph into Friday evening. The strongest winds of the event occurred for coastal NE FL Saturday morning, Nov. 6th, with sustained speeds 45-55 mph and gusts 60-70 mph. A peak wind gust of 68 mph was measured at the St. Augustine C-MAN station Saturday morning 11/6 around 06:30 am (peak sustained wind was 55 mph from the north) with a gust of 70 mph at 5:37 am at the Huguenot Park mesonet site. Moderate tidal flooding occurred along the local Atlantic coast with inundation of 2-3 feet.
episodes.163755: A broad surface low pressure and frontal system pushed across the central and southern portions of the Florida peninsula while an upper-level jet moved through the same region. This combined with very high moisture led to strong training storms and caused heavy rainfall and flooding to occur across portions of eastern South FL.
episodes.163757: A broad surface low pressure and frontal system pushed across the central and southern portions of the Florida peninsula while an upper-level jet moved through the same region. This combined with very high moisture led to strong thunderstorms with strong winds across portions of the Atlantic waters.
episodes.163965: A nearby front and unstable conditions ahead of an area of low pressure over the Gulf of Mexico aided development of a band of showers and a few thunderstorms over the peninsula. As the band reached the east coast, one of the showers produced strong wind gusts at New Smyrna Beach.
episodes.163968: A nearby front and unstable conditions ahead of an area of low pressure over the Gulf of Mexico aided development of a very slow-moving band of showers and a few thunderstorms. Flooding and road closures occurred within Volusia County, primarily affecting portions of Daytona Beach and Port Orange.

events.narrative: A trained spotter along with various members of the public reported street flooding across portions of Miami-Dade County due to heavy rainfall. Rainfall estimates around 2-4 inches. The intersection of Bird Road and Le Jeune Road had standing water exceeding the curb, there was street flooding along Stanford Drive on the University of Miami's campus, street flooding along North Greenway Drive and Cordova Street in Coral Gables, and street flooding on Granada Boulevard and South Greenway Drive where flooding was over the curbs and halfway up car tires.

An NWS employee and various members of the public reported flooding in portions of the City of Miami near Biscayne Bay due to heavy rainfall. Significant flooding in the Edgewater neighborhood caused water to enter the first level of a condominium building on NE 30th Terrace and causing the elevators to stop working. Reports of street flooding in Downtown Miami near Biscayne Boulevard and NE 15th Street with water reaching over the sidewalk and halfway up car tires. Significant street flooding also occurred near S. Miami Avenue and 9th street and also SE 1st Avenue and SE 9th Street where water exceeded curbs and was flowing down streets, with water passing car tires. ||Rainfall in the general area was around 3 inches, most of it falling in only 1 hour leading to very high rainfall rates. The presence of king tides during this time period may have exacerbated the flooding in these areas.

events.narrative: A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 43 mph (37 knots) was measured by the WXflow mesonet station XGVT located at Government Cut at 618 AM EDT. This was preceded by a wind gust of 42 mph (36 knots) at 608 AM EDT. Anemometer height is 75 feet.

A trained spotter reported flooding due to heavy rain on West Sample Road near I-95. The right lane was flooded and a couple of cars stalled in the flood waters.||Rainfall in the general area was around 3 inches, most of it falling in only 1 hour leading to very high rainfall rates.
About 4.25 inches was observed as the storm total rainfall over the past 24 hours.

About 4.42 inches was observed by personal weather station cypres knoll south KFLPALMC130. Rain began falling around 5 am and then heavy rain began around noon and continued to around 9 pm. Surrounding rain gages ranged from 2.5 to 3.5 inches for their total rainfall amounts.
About 4.81 inches of rainfall was observed by personal weather station n4ssg dock wx KFLFLAGL40. Rain began falling around 5 am and then heavy rain began around 1 pm and continued to around 9 pm.

A very slow-moving front produced persistent heavy rains across portion of Volusia County. Twenty-four hour rain totals were 6-10 inches, however most of the rain fell in less than 12-hours, impacting Daytona Beach and Port Orange. As much as 5-6 inches accumulated between 1500 and 1800 LST. Numerous roadways were flooded, with as much as 1-2 feet of standing water in some localized areas, resulting in road closures.
